findings.title: Date overrides bypass booking and calendar conflicts
findings.body: When a slot falls within a date override, this returns `true` before checking `busy`. Date overrides should replace the user's normal working hours, not make an already-booked or calendar-busy slot bookable. For fixed hosts in round-robin events, this can expose conflicting slots and allow double-bookings.

findings.title: Override validation allows slots extending past the override
findings.body: This rejects a slot only when it ends before the override starts or starts after the override ends. A slot that starts inside the override but ends after it is accepted, as is one starting exactly at the override end. For example, a 60-minute slot starting at 10:30 passes a 10:00–11:00 override. This can advertise times when a fixed host is unavailable.

findings.title: Split working hours incorrectly reject valid slots
findings.body: The `.find()` rejects a slot if it is outside *any* working-hours interval on that day. With separate intervals such as 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a 14:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the first interval, even though it fits the second. Check whether the slot fits at least one interval instead; otherwise users with split schedules lose valid availability.
